newsitem.title: USA: Calif. voters divided on tax initiative - poll.
newsitem.headline: Calif. voters divided on tax initiative - poll.

text.p: California voters are evenly divided on a controversial tax initiative that would make it more difficult for local governments to raise revenue, according to a Field Institute poll released Tuesday.

After they were read a summary of the initiative's official description, 40 percent of likely voters said they intended to vote for Proposition 218, while 39 percent said they intended to vote against the measure.
Twenty-one percent were undecided, the Field poll found.

The poll was based on a survey conducted Oct 7 to 9 among a representative statewide sample of 505 likely voters. The margin of error was plus or minus 4.5 percentage points, the non-partisan Field Institute said. Proposition 218 would

require that a majority of local voters in an election approve any increase in general taxes. It would also limit local government's use of fees and assessments. Some municipal analysts maintain the initiative could have a devastating effect on local government finance.
The October results mirrored Field poll findings in September.
